title: Survivorship Bias & Regime-Shift Autopsy: How a Backtest That Shone Dies Live
content: A strategy that backtests brilliantly on the current cross-section of surviving assets carries a compounding lie: every bankruptcy, delisting, and acquisition has been silently excised, so the historical universe is filtered by future outcomes, and the strategy has never actually traded a loser into zero. When a regime shift arrives — most acutely in rate-shock or credit-stress environments where defaults cluster — live performance craters precisely because the tail events the backtest never saw are now the majority of the return distribution. The canonical fix is point-in-time universe construction: at each historical bar the eligible set must contain only assets that were tradeable on that date, including eventual failures, sourced from a survivorship-free database such as CRSP or Compustat with delisting returns applied. Separately, strategies optimised inside a single hospitable regime (e.g., low-vol, low-rate 2010-2021) are doubly exposed: even with a clean universe, in-sample parameter fit will not transfer to the new regime, producing a second wave of live underperformance that looks like alpha decay but is structural model mis-specification.
lesson: Survivorship bias is not just a return-inflation error — it is a regime-invisibility error: the failures that define a stressed regime are exactly the observations that were removed, so the strategy is blind to the environment where it will be most severely tested; point-in-time universe construction and multi-regime walk-forward testing are non-optional before any live deployment.
